title: Immer
description: Immutability made easy with structural sharing.

data.text: Immer lets you write mutative code that produces immutable updates. It uses proxies to track changes and produce a new state.

data.title: Immer produce

data.text: Write Mutable Code, Get Immutable Results

Immer wraps an object in a draft. You modify the draft as if it were mutable, and Immer produces a new object with only the changed paths copied — structural sharing keeps the rest by reference. That gives readable reducers without hand-written spreads.

data.title: A reducer with produce

data.text: A nested update with spreads has to rebuild every level: `{ ...state, user: { ...state.user, address: { ...state.user.address, city } } }`. The deeper the tree, the easier it is to forget a level and mutate by accident. Immer writes the same change in one line and guarantees a new reference at each changed level, which is what memoization needs to detect the change.

data.title: In a Redux slice and with useReducer
Immer is in Redux Toolkit already
data.text: If you use Redux Toolkit you are writing Immer reducers without naming it. The standalone `produce` is useful for local state and custom stores. Remember that Immer returns a frozen draft by default, so a later accidental mutation of the returned object throws in strict mode — a feature, not a bug.
